parsed.diagnosis: Current FDIR allows only one isolation. Logs show first mild friction fault with residual ~4.5e-04 Nm trips detector and consumes the slot, then a later severe friction or torque-derate fault cannot be isolated. Control remains on three wheels including the badly degraded wheel, leading to attitude loss or wheel saturation, while no-isolation runs stay safe. This is policy-induced lock-in, dominant in rw_friction+rw_friction cases.
parsed.rule_in_words: Re-admit an isolated wheel after its uncommanded torque residual stays at or below 0.0003 Nm continuously for 1800 s, freeing the single isolation slot for a later fault.
parsed.rationale: First mild fault still isolated promptly, preserving current protection. If residual was transient or mild, prolonged healthy uncommanded monitoring returns it to control and restores four-wheel redundancy. When a second hard fault appears, the slot is free to isolate the truly degraded wheel, restoring healthy three-wheel control. Late violations at 7000-11000 s leave time for 1800 s qualification plus re-isolation. This directly addresses lock-in in friction-friction and friction-derate sequences without changing detection thresholds.
parsed.why_no_regressions: No early behavior changes: detection thresholds, persistence, and first isolation identical to current policy. No swaps to worse wheels and no safe-mode timing changes that regressed before. Re-admission needs 1800 s continuously healthy at 0.0003 Nm, so persistently faulty wheels stay isolated and single-fault clean runs are unchanged. Only long-healthy mild wheels are returned, restoring redundancy.
parsed.ideal_rule_if_unconstrained: Ideal would continuously rank wheels by filtered residual and always control on healthiest three with unlimited isolations, plus confirmed-fault latching and momentum-based safe entry.
